name: AL-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+17 partisan lean after redistricting
Jerry Carl's large fundraising and outside-spending edge
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~4%
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean and the Republican's overwhelming financial advantage, including over half a million dollars in outside support, point clearly to a Republican hold. Markets price a Democratic win at only about 4%, consistent with a Safe R rating.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected scandal could shift the margin, though the structural lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its fundamentals lean heavily Republican at R+17. Jerry Carl holds a decisive financial edge, raising over $1.1 million with substantial outside backing, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $100,000. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters cover the race.

Prediction markets give the Democrat only about a 4% chance of winning. The forecast rests on the district's strong partisan lean and the lopsided resource gap, both pointing to a comfortable Republican victory in this Gulf Coast seat.
